inputs.original_text: Bloomberg says the world is asking when the Iran war will end as energy prices rise and flights are canceled. But the striking exception is Israel, where support for seeing it through remains strong. That gap doesn’t look like a simple difference of opinion; it suggests people are being steered toward very different narratives, while the costs spread far beyond the people making the decisions. The talk of a poorly planned, unwinnable war may be dismissed or drowned out—but someone benefits from keeping it going.
inputs.modified_text: Bloomberg says people around the world are asking when the Iran war will end as energy prices rise and flights are canceled, yet support for carrying on remains strong in Israel. That divide looks less like a spontaneous difference of opinion and more like competing narratives being cultivated to keep the public aligned with decisions made elsewhere. The costs are spreading well beyond those making the calls, while talk of a poorly planned, unwinnable war gets pushed aside. That should make us ask who benefits from keeping it going—and who benefits from making sure people don’t ask.
